newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's 1996 EBR 437 mln punts-Finance Ministry.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's 1996 EBR 437 mln punts-Finance Ministry.

text.p: Ireland's Exchequer Borrowing Requirement (EBR) totalled 437 million punts or 1.2 percent of GNP in 1996 compared with 627 million punts in 1995, the Irish finance ministry said on Friday.
The 1996 outturn undershoots the government's target of 729 million Irish pounds by 292 million.
Economists' forecasts for the figure had ranged from 250 to 400 million punts.
The finance ministry said the current budget surplus was 292 million punts
This was 374 milion punts better thanthe original budget target and is by far the largest current surplus ever recorded, the ministry said.
Borrowing for capital purposes was 729 million Irish pounds, 82 million above the government's original target.

The General Government Deficit, the measurement used for the Maastricht criteria on EMU membership, is estimated to have turned out at about 1.0 percent of GDP compared to a post-budget of 2.6 percent, the ministry said.

"This outturn will easily maintain Ireland's position among the strongest fiscal performers in the EU. The deficit has now been comfortably below the 3.0 percent Maastricht ceiling for eight consecutive years," the ministry said.

"Looking forward to 1997, we are clearly well placed to comfortably secure the fiscal criteria for participation in EMU, which requires a General Government Deficit of no more than 3.0 percent of GDP and a continuation of the decline in our debt/GDP ratio," it said. -- Dublin Newsroom +353-1-661-3377...
